subject: Exec clearance request — LumaHealth 3yr anchor & renewal failsafe
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Erin Park <erin@lumahealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-18T09:12:00Z
Subject: Proposal — 3yr term anchor, uplift cap and renewal protection

Hi Erin,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday — excited about the potential fit between LumaHealth and Redwood. Per our call, attached is a concise proposal that reflects the commercial guardrails we discussed: a 3-year commitment with an "anchor" price for years 1–2, a limited uplift in year 3, and a renewal protection clause to reduce churn risk for you. High level: 

- Term: 36 months (start = date of execution).
- Price lock: fixed unit rates for months 1–24.
- Uplift cap: maximum 7% list-stated uplift in year 3 (applied to base rate only).
- Renewal protection: at renewal we will offer an optional one-time extension at the committed blended price + uplift cap; price increases beyond this are limited and only apply if consumption tiers move to the next bracket.
- Usage carveouts: burst/overage remains billable but protected by monthly overage credits for the first 90 days post-go-live.

I know you asked about a firmer uplift cap and stronger renewal parity. We can consider tightening the uplift cap if we get a minimum annual committed usage band and a DocuSign amendment to lock the commercial terms. I copied Aditya and Karthik to keep Deal Desk in the loop.

Next steps: if you can confirm acceptance or send redlines by EOD Friday (2028-07-20) we can hold the pricing and route for internal approval. Attached: Redwood_MultiYear_Term_Proposal_v3.pdf (proposal summary).

Thanks,

Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

---
Attachment: Redwood_MultiYear_Term_Proposal_v3.pdf (pdf, 3 pages)

From: Erin Park <erin@lumahealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: LumaHealth Legal <legal@lumahealth.com>
Date: 2028-07-18T13:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Proposal — 3yr term anchor, uplift cap and renewal protection

Thanks, Stephanie. Appreciate the clear summary and the tight timeline. A few notes from Procurement and Legal after a quick skim: 

1) Uplift cap — procurement is pushing for a 3% max uplift in year 3 rather than 7%. They cite budget predictability and a multi-year vendor strategy.
2) Renewal protection — we want a renewal parity clause that explicitly states our renewal band cannot increase beyond the committed blended rate + uplift cap and that any step increases must be tied to additional features (not general market inflation).
3) Minimum commitment — we can accept a minimum committed usage that supports a tighter uplift cap; will propose a band in our redlines.

I'm attaching a redline doc with comments: Luma_Redlines_v1.pdf. Procurement has a hard milestone: our finance committee meets on 2028-07-25; we need final pricing and legal terms in advance to get on the agenda. If Redwood can sign off on a 3% uplift cap with the minimum commitment and a simple renewal parity clause, we can move to signature quickly.

Can we get an internal confirmation on whether Redwood can make that concession?

Thanks,
Erin Park
Sr. Director, Procurement | LumaHealth
erin@lumahealth.com

---
Attachment: Luma_Redlines_v1.pdf (pdf, 2 pages)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-19T08:05:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Luma redlines — request for exec clearance (3% uplift ask)

Team — forwarding Luma's redlines and procurement ask. Erin is asking for a 3% uplift cap in year 3 (down from our proposed 7%) in exchange for a committed usage band. Key facts and ask: 

- Account: LumaHealth (mid-market healthcare platform; strategic in patient engagement vertical).
- Proposed concession: reduce year-3 uplift cap to 3% if Luma signs a minimum annual committed usage of $480k ARR (equivalent to the mid-tier usage band in our pricing schedule) and executes a 36-month amendment.
- Expected margin impact: preliminary estimate is ~6% reduction in lifetime gross margin vs proposal (Naomi, see attached memo for details).
- Strategic rationale: Luma is referenceable in the healthcare vertical and likely to expand into three other product lines within 18 months; faster time-to-contract moves them into onboarding earlier this quarter.

Attachments: Approval_Memo_Luma.pdf (includes P&L sketch, risk points, recommended guardrails).

Suggested internal guardrails if we accept the 3% uplift cap: 
- DocuSign amendment executed before pricing is locked; no back-dating.
- 12-month minimum billing ramp clause: if usage falls below 60% of committed band in any rolling 12-month window, Redwood can re-open pricing for next renewal.
- Limit on total one-time concession: any accelerator/credits must be < $30k and pre-approved by Finance.

Requesting an explicit exec clearance to accept the 3% uplift cap under the guardrails above. If we get a green light, I will communicate acceptance to Erin and instruct Legal to prepare the amendment. Timing is tight — Procurement needs a confirmed commercial position by 2028-07-21 COB to stay on the 7/25 finance committee agenda.

TIA for quick review — note I'm flexible on the exact minimum ARR threshold if Finance flags issues, but we need to preserve the principal of the committed band to justify the uplift concession.

— Stephanie

---
Attachment: Approval_Memo_Luma.pdf (pdf, 4 pages, includes margin analysis and recommended approval matrix)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-20T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Luma redlines — request for exec clearance (3% uplift ask)

Thanks for the memo, Stephanie. Reviewed the P&L sketch and the proposed guardrails. Finance is willing to approve the 3% uplift cap provided the following conditions are met: 

1) Minimum committed ARR must be documented at $500k (slightly higher than your ask) with a 36-month commitment.
2) Accelerator/credits cap stands at $25k (we need room for implementation credits but want to limit impact).
3) 12-month minimum billing ramp clause as proposed (if they drop below 60% of committed band we reserve the right to re-price at next renewal).
4) Legal must agree to a renewal parity clause that ties any renewal uplift to feature add-ons and explicitly excludes general market inflation adjustments.

If Sales accepts the $500k ARR threshold and the $25k credit cap, Finance will sign off and we will route to Legal for a fast-track amendment. Please confirm and I'll flag to Legal and Deal Desk to prepare the DocuSign amendment template and approval stamp.

Naomi Feldman
Head of Finance | Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
